transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Time: 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Lucas Reed (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Ember CTO), Dev Patel (Lead ML Eng), Anita Gomez (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Ember Logistics is evaluating Redwood to replace an in-house endpoint for routing and chat. They have strict p95 latency targets and mixed workload requiring streaming and large batch throughput. Interested in Dedicated for predictability but want to validate hosted performance first.

[00:00] Lucas (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today. Quick intros - I'm Lucas, AE on the Redwood infra team, with Priya who is our systems SE.
[00:06] Maya: Hi, Maya Chen, CTO at Ember. Dev and Anita from infra/ML are on.
[00:10] Priya (SE): Hi, yeah, hi all. Quick agenda - want to understand your current latency/throughput targets, concurrency, streaming needs and security constraints. We'll then talk through hosted vs dedicated vs private and propose a benchmark plan.
[00:20] Dev: Great. So top-line, we power two features: a live operator chat that needs sub-300ms p95 for perceived real-time UX, and a nightly batch scoring pipeline that needs to process ~15k tokens/sec sustained for model scoring.
[00:34] Anita: Our traffic shape is spiky during morning and evening windows - roughly 3k concurrent open websocket connections during peak for the chat, but individual messages are short (20-120 tokens typically). Batch runs are off-peak and we can schedule.
[00:47] Priya: Helpful. When you say p95 sub-300ms, is that for end-to-end user-visible latency including network + client, or for inference alone?
[00:55] Maya: Good question - that's user-visible, so we'd like inference p95 to be under 200-220ms to give some headroom for network and client rendering.
[01:04] Priya: Got it. That's doable depending on model size and routing. Are you using a proprietary model or a standard open model?
[01:11] Dev: We're on a finetuned open-architecture model roughly 13B parameters, quantized to 4-bit for cost. We also are experimenting with a 7B distilled for low-latency routes.
[01:22] Priya: OK that helps. A couple of clarifications - for streaming, do you need token-by-token streaming (human chat feel) or chunked streaming?
[01:29] Maya: Token-by-token ideally. We want immediate partials as operators type. But if chunked streaming helps guarantee p95, we'd consider 100-200ms chunking.
[01:38] Priya: Understood. For concurrency, you said 3k open websockets, how many simultaneous inference requests do you expect?
[01:45] Dev: At peak about 400-600 simultaneous in-flight requests; average messages per active user is low but bursts happen. So concurrency target p95 should be evaluated around 600 concurrent.
[01:56] Lucas: To confirm, desired SLO: inference p95 < 220ms at 600 concurrent for token-by-token streaming with 20-120 token ranges. Batch throughput target: 15k tokens/sec sustained for scoring jobs. Anything else?
[02:10] Maya: Also want deterministic fallbacks - if a dedicated pool is saturated we need automatic route to a cheaper hosted model with clear latency bounds.
[02:18] Priya: We do smart routing + automatic fallbacks. Our Dedicated product gives predictable throughput but you can configure policy to fallback to hosted compatible variants. We can demo that in the pilot.
[02:27] Dev: On security, we need SOC2 + ISO and want customer-managed KMS for private deployments; for hosted we'd need encryption at rest with CMK and audit logs.
[02:37] Anita: Also SSO integration and RBAC - our infra team needs to enforce least-privilege for token issuance.
[02:44] Lucas: We have SOC2 and ISO docs, and Redwood Private supports bring-your-own-KMS + VPC peering. Hosted supports CMK with audit exports; we can share the security pack.
[02:55] Maya: Good. On benchmarking - what would you need from us to prove the p95 and token/sec claims?
[03:02] Priya: Ideally: example prompts and message distribution CSV (we need token lengths distribution), a staging VPC for Private/Dedicated pilot, and permission to run a 2-hour load test against hosted and dedicated variants. We'll provide benchmark scripts that measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and tokens/sec.
[03:16] Dev: We can provide prompts and a traffic dump. For the staging VPC, we'd need a runbook for onboarding - can you support a short-lived VPN/peering?
[03:24] Priya: Yes, we can do VPC peering and a short-lived staging cluster. We typically provision a trial Dedicated pool for two weeks for pilots.
[03:31] Anita: Important: For private pilot we need to know hardware - we are evaluating Ampere Altra vs Nvidia H100. Do you have performance profiles?
[03:38] Priya: We keep a model catalog with performance profiles - those are approximate - we can map your 13B quantized model to our kernel selections. H100 will generally give better single-request latency, while Ampere can be more cost-efficient for batching. We'll include kernel/hardware recommendations in the bench plan.
[03:53] Lucas: Quick note: quantization/4-bit will affect throughput and latency; sometimes 4-bit on Ampere has different kernel paths causing slightly higher p95. We'll highlight that in the report.
[04:05] Maya: For streaming, how do you handle KV cache for multi-turn? We need memory efficiency to handle many concurrent sessions.
[04:12] Priya: We use KV cache sharding and prefix caching; we can also pin tokens in cache for active sessions to reduce recompute on partial tokens. There are tradeoffs with memory footprint vs latency; we'll outline options.
[04:24] Dev: Any chance you can show a quick synthetic result for a 7B distilled model now? Even ballpark numbers?
[04:30] Priya: Ballpark for 7B distilled on dedicated H100 with optimized kernels: downstream p95 for single-turn streaming with small tokens could be ~80-120ms; on hosted we usually see ~110-180ms depending on network. For 13B quantized on Ampere it might be 180-320ms p95. These are rough - pilot will validate.
[04:51] Maya: That aligns with our expectations. For batch scoring, what's your approach to hitting sustained 15k tokens/sec? Do you recommend big batch workers or horizontal scaling?
[04:59] Priya: For sustained tokens/sec, we leverage continuous batching and multi-request concurrency on Dedicated to hit high tokens/sec. Autoscaling helps, but Dedicated capacity gives predictable slots so you can reserve throughput. We'll show cost estimates: many customers run large batch windows with fewer large nodes rather than many small ones.
[05:15] Dev: And how do you measure tokens/sec for mixed workloads with streaming? We can't sacrifice chat latency for batch throughput.
[05:22] Priya: You should separate routing policies: keep chat on latency-optimized pool, route batch to throughput-optimized pool (or run at off-peak). Smart routing ensures batch doesn't impact p95 for chat.
[05:31] Anita: Any mention of telemetry? We need token-level cost, p95 per route, and per-model dashboards.
[05:37] Lucas: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency percentiles, and alerting. We'll include screenshots in the follow-up.
[05:44] Maya: Good. On procurement timeline, we aim to decide in 3-4 weeks after pilot. Security review will be parallel.
[05:52] Lucas: Sounds reasonable. Proposed next steps: we'll send the benchmark plan, security docs, and pricing; you send prompts and traffic distribution; schedule the pilot next week.
[05:59] Maya: Yes. Also for acceptance criteria: p95 inference under 220ms for chat at 600 concurrency and sustained 15k tokens/sec for batch with <5% error rate. If we hit those, we'll move to Dedicated procurement.
[06:12] Priya: Noted. I'll put those acceptance criteria into the plan.
[06:16] Dev: One minor item - we want auto-scaling cooldowns to be configurable per route; some batch jobs spike and we don't want oscillation.
[06:24] Priya: You can set autoscaling windows on Dedicated and we have burst policies for short spikes.
[06:29] Anita: We'll need an escalation contact for pilot support.
[06:32] Lucas: I'll be primary, Priya will be SE support. We'll include a Slack channel invite for the pilot.
[06:37] Lucas: Anything else?
[06:39] Maya: No, that's it. Thanks all.
[06:41] Lucas: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the benchmark plan and pricing.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions: 'KV cache' heard as 'K V cash' in auto captions; 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes appears as 'Redwood dedicate' in captions. Speakers occasionally truncated.

End of call.
